text:
alex: Heads-up — we're seeing ~3x late events from EU ingestion during 03:00-06:00 UTC and the recompute backlog is spiking. Console shows lots of 'high' rehydrate jobs queued. Can we quickly bias routing so targeted replays use Dedicated slots (or a preemptible lane) and deprioritize debug/low-value replays? cc @devin @maria

devin: Do we know if this is genuine late-arrival or duplicate replays? Any sample keys/rows? If it's the former we can favor fresh-data lanes; if duplicates we should dedupe before scheduling.

alex: Quick snippet from the late ingest logs (example keys redacted):
```
INGEST: partition=eu-1 hour=2026-02-14T04:00Z event_lag_sec=7200 key=*** status=arrived
REPLAY-QUEUE: enqueue job=targeted-backfill tenant=acme-corp window=1h reason=late-ingest
```
We have many of these across multiple partitions, not just dupes. Also seeing long tail in per-token latency when the backlog hits batch thresholds.

replay-bot: Started targeted-backfill job id=rb-20260214-001 (tenant=acme-corp) — estimated tokens=2.4M — https://replays/redwood/job/rb-20260214-001 :rocket:

sam: Short-term hack: we can add a temporary label on the replay API that the scheduler recognizes, e.g. `priority_hint=soft_high` and route those to dedicated-slot pools. Example curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api/replays -d '{"tenant":"acme-corp","window":"1h","priority_hint":"soft_high"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```
That avoids touching quota math but still nudges routing.

maria: Console UX ask — can we expose a checkbox on the targeted-replay modal: "Prefer low-latency pool (may incur reserved capacity)" with a cost estimate next to it? Ops and SRE need the estimated token cost and predicted wait-time. Right now people click 'run' blindly.

devin: For medium-term, suggest adding a preemptible lane configuration in routing policies:
```
"routing_policies": [
  {"name":"preemptible_replay","priority":30,"pool":"spot-dedicated","preemptible":true}
]
```
That lets us route non-critical replays to cheaper GPUs when available, fall back to shared pool otherwise. Need to check fallout for canary rollouts.

lina: Who owns the small UX + API change? I can take the console change if someone pairs on the backend label. Otherwise we should avoid partials that confuse customers.

alex: I'll own the backend label + scheduler recognition. plan: 1) deploy `priority_hint` parsing to scheduler as a feature flag, 2) expose single checkbox in console (maria/lina pair), 3) run a canary for one tenant for 4 hours. Can someone request a short quota exemption for dedicated slots for the canary?

ops: Please open a quota ticket with the `rb-tool` CLI: `rb-tool quota request --tenant acme-corp --pool dedicated-eu --hours 4 --tokens 2500000` — include the thread link and desired start time. We'll triage within 30m. Also watch SLO alerts for latent token spikes.

sam: One caution: `priority_hint` must not bypass billing or telemetry counts. We should mark those replays with `meta.routing_hint=true` so billing & telemetry still record them as normal.

alex: Agree. We'll add `meta.routing_hint` in scheduler events. Also adding a small safety: if queue depth > 10k, automatically downgrade `soft_high` to `background` to avoid starving foreground traffic.

maria: UX note — add an inline estimate: "Estimated cost: ~$20 — Expected wait: <5m on dedicated lane (best effort)". Hide estimate if quota exemption needed.

replay-bot: rb-20260214-001 status=running workers=6 pool=dedicated-eu

lina: I'll start the console PR after alex posts the API contract.

alex: I'll post the scheduler PR in 15m and toggle the ff in staging. Planning canary run at 09:00 UTC (09:00 scheduled start). If observed latency >5x or error-rate rises, we revert routing flag. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ops: Noted — we'll stand by for the ticket and monitor. If you need emergency rollbacks, ping #eng-oncall.

alex: Canary started 09:00 UTC — posting outcomes in this thread. If this works, we can generalize routing_policies for other regions.
